name: CapCut Compound Graphics Workflow
use_when: A CapCut or NLE timeline contains many text, shape, map, chart, image, and SFX layers that need clean organization.
An infographic section needs internal retiming while moving as one scene in the main timeline.
The agent needs to translate CapCut compound clips into nested sequences, precomps, or components.
A heavy overlay or masked-clip section causes playback lag and needs to be isolated before returning to the main timeline.
A documentary parallax scene needs foreground cutouts, background motion, and text layers to move as organized nested units.
A CapCut sticker, text layer, or simple graphic needs access to video-style animation options that are unavailable on the original layer type.
avoid_when: The section has only one or two layers and nesting would make edits harder.
The compound is used to hide messy naming or unclear timing rather than organize a stable scene.
The project requires direct handoff where every layer must remain visible in the top-level timeline.
Timing is still so unstable that pre-rendering or nesting would create extra replacement work.

timeline_pattern.pattern: build_scene_layers_long -> align_internal_animations -> trim_layer_ends -> compound_clip -> move_transform_fade_as_scene -> reopen_compound_for_internal_timing
timeline_pattern.build_long_rule: Give elements extra duration while designing, then trim the compound to the actual animation.
timeline_pattern.scene_rule: Each compound should represent one idea: intro, map, chart, document, word focus, or final collage.
timeline_pattern.editability_rule: Name compounds and keep internal layers accessible for retiming.
timeline_pattern.heavy_overlay_rule: For laggy CapCut edits, isolate one heavy clip or section, keep enough handles, build overlays/effects there, then replace or nest it back into the main timeline.
timeline_pattern.animation_unlock_rule: When a sticker or text layer lacks the needed animation controls, create a compound clip from that layer, then apply video-clip animations or scene transforms to the compound while preserving access to the original layer inside.
timeline_pattern.attribute_copy_rule: When copying foreground location/size motion to a background or text compound, treat it as a starting point and reduce the copied values so depth remains visible.

motion.rule: Apply whole-scene transforms to the compound only after internal layer timing works.

keyframe_values.intro_build_length: Create uncertain intro scenes around 8-10 seconds, then trim to the finished 3-6 seconds when entrances are complete.
keyframe_values.scene_exit: Use fade, slide, or scale exit on the compound rather than cutting all internal layers harshly.
keyframe_values.compound_easing: Use cubic/eased curves for whole-scene pan, scale, and rotation.
keyframe_values.heavy_overlay_handles: Keep full clip length or extra handles when isolating a heavy clip so transition work remains possible.
keyframe_values.animation_unlock: Use a compound wrapper for text/sticker layers only when a normal keyframe or built-in animation cannot create the needed behavior.
keyframe_values.parallax_background: After pasting foreground motion attributes onto a background, lower the scale and position changes so the background drifts more subtly than the cutouts.

sound.rule: Keep SFX either inside the compound only when they belong permanently to that scene, or on top-level tracks when final mix control matters.

captions.rule: Keep captions outside graphic compounds unless they are part of the designed graphic, so accessibility text remains easy to move.

color.rule: Apply scene-wide color/texture effects at compound level only after checking internal text and data readability.

implementation.ffmpeg: Represent each compound as a reusable composition or intermediate render with source layer metadata retained in project JSON.
implementation.remotion: Model compounds as named components with internal sequences and top-level scene transforms.
implementation.blender: Use scene collections or strips in the Video Sequence Editor for grouped infographic scenes.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Highlight section layers, trim with W when useful, create compound clips, double-click to retime internals, and return to main timeline for scene-level transforms. If a sticker/text layer needs video-style animations, create a compound from it and apply the animation to the compound. For documentary parallax, compound cutout sequences and text groups separately, copy location/size attributes only as a starting point, then reduce background/text motion so depth remains. For heavy overlay edits, work on one clip in its own project or compound, export/replace it, and keep final transitions/SFX in the main project.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use nested sequences; in After Effects, use precomps. Keep top-level sequence organized by scene while preserving source layers inside nests/precomps. For laggy sections, use Render and Replace or intermediates while retaining the source nest for revisions.

common_mistakes: Compounding too early before layer timing is understandable.
Leaving compounds unnamed so the final export range is confusing.
Applying scene-level effects that make internal text unreadable.
Putting captions inside a graphic compound where they cannot avoid later collisions.
Forgetting to reopen and retime internal layers after changing compound duration.
Compounding a sticker or text layer just to use a flashy animation when a precise manual keyframe would be cleaner.
Overtrimming a heavy overlay subproject so the replacement clip has no transition handles.
Pasting identical motion onto background, foreground, and text compounds so the whole scene moves like one flat layer.
qc: Does each compound represent one clear graphic idea?
Are compound clips named and still editable?
Do internal layer timings still match narration after trimming the compound?
Are captions kept movable unless they are part of the graphic design?
Do whole-scene transforms preserve all edges, text, maps, charts, and SFX sync?
If a heavy section was rendered or replaced, are the original layers retained and enough handles preserved?
If a compound is used to unlock animation options, is the source sticker/text still editable inside it?
When attributes are copied between compounds, were background/text transforms reduced enough to preserve depth?
